chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr al-Wasiti, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When a man divorces his wife while he is absent, and the proof is established for that, then her waiting period (iddah) is from the day he divorced her.
ai.seo_question: When does the waiting period begin for a woman whose husband is absent at the time of divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural aspect of divorce (talaq) where the husband is absent, establishing that the waiting period (iddah) commences upon the judicial confirmation of the divorce rather than the moment of utterance. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling ensures legal certainty for the woman by anchoring the start of iddah to the date the evidence is presented and accepted, preventing disputes over the exact timing of the husband's declaration. It highlights the importance of witness testimony (bayyinah) in validating the divorce event when direct observation is not possible.
